label: History
value: Phillips was the schoolteacher in Avonlea
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolteacher in Avonlea during Anne Shirley's early years at Green Gables. During his tenure, he openly courted one of his older pupils, Prissy Andrews, causing much gossip in the community and leading him to neglect the rest of the school. He antagonized Anne Shirley on several occasions, notably misspelling her name on the blackboard, punishing her for being late by forcing her to sit next to Gilbert Blythe, and humiliating her for losing her temper. These incidents prompted Anne to refuse to attend school for a time. Later, he organized a test class for pupils preparing for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations, which included Anne and Gilbert. At the end of the school year, he gave a surprisingly emotional farewell speech before leaving Avonlea permanently.

label: History
value: Captain Jim welcomes Gilbert Blythe into his lighthouse
unit: James Boyd, universally known as Captain Jim, spent most of his life as a sailor before retiring to become the keeper of the Four Winds Light on Prince Edward Island. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe move to their 'house of dreams' nearby, Captain Jim immediately befriends them, welcoming them into his light-house and sharing his colorful life stories. He introduces Anne to Leslie Moore and takes a deep interest in helping Leslie through her tragic life circumstances. Captain Jim keeps a beloved 'life-book' filled with notes of his maritime adventures, which he long hopes will be published. He entrusts these memoirs to Owen Ford, a visiting author, who turns the Captain's life experiences into a successful novel. Shortly after seeing his life's book completed and witnessing Leslie Moore's newfound happiness, Captain Jim passes away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse.

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott was transformed back into a handsome man.
unit: Marshall Elliott is a long-time resident of Four Winds who made a famous political vow in his youth never to shave or cut his hair until the Liberals won the election. Because the Conservatives remained in power for decades, Marshall's hair and beard grew to extraordinary lengths, making him one of the coastline's notable eccentrics. He held a long-standing affection for Miss Cornelia Bryant, but she refused to marry a man who looked like a tramp. When the Liberals finally won a general election, Marshall promptly went to the barber, cut his hair, shaved his beard, and bought a new suit of clothes. Transformed back into a handsome, respectable man, he immediately proposed to Miss Cornelia Bryant. She accepted him, and the two were happily married, settling down together in Four Winds.
